# pip-audit ignore list - Localization OS TMS (compliance gap G-08).
#
# WHAT THIS IS. One vulnerability-advisory ID per line that the CI `dep-audit`
# job passes to `pip-audit --ignore-vuln`. The audit runs against the LOCKED
# runtime tree (requirements.lock) and FAILS on any advisory NOT listed here.
# This file is the escape hatch: an advisory is pinned here so the gate stays
# green while the fix (a dependency upgrade) is scheduled as separate work.
#
# FORMAT. `<ADVISORY-ID>  # owner=<name> expires=YYYY-MM-DD reason=<short>`. Blank lines and lines whose first
# token starts with `#` are ignored by the CI parser (it reads field 1 only).
# Every entry needs owner, expiry, reason, reachability=, and fixed= version. verify_release_lock rejects stale
# entries in CI, including scheduled audits. Expiry is inclusive (UTC in CI).
# LOAD-BEARING: this file MUST stay LF (it is pinned eol=lf in .gitattributes). The
# CI parser is `awk '$1 !~ /^#/ && NF {print $1}'`; under Linux gawk a CRLF line
# leaves a trailing \r on field 1, so a bare-ID line becomes "PYSEC-...\r" and the
# --ignore-vuln no longer matches - the gate would fail on an already-pinned CVE.
#
# HOW TO CLEAR AN ENTRY (the manual lock-regen step). Dependabot bumps the pin in
# requirements.txt but does NOT touch requirements.lock, and this job audits the
# LOCK - so an entry here clears only when a human refreshes the lock:
#   1. Upgrade the affected package to (at least) the "Fix Versions" pip-audit
#      reports, in requirements.txt (mind the load-bearing pins - e.g. starlette's
#      floor is set by the pinned fastapi, so its cluster needs a coordinated bump).
#   2. Use the clean Python 3.13 PowerShell recipe in docs/DEPLOY.md, keeping
#      uvicorn[standard] in requirements.txt. Exact base refresh commands:
#      & .\.lock-refresh\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
#      & .\.lock-refresh\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
#      $basePins = @(& .\.lock-refresh\Scripts\python.exe -m pip freeze | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^(pywin32|uvloop)==' })
#      $basePins += 'pywin32==312 ; sys_platform == "win32"'
#      $sortedPins = [Collections.Generic.SortedDictionary[string,string]]::new([StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
#      foreach ($pin in $basePins) { $sortedPins.Add(($pin -split '==')[0], $pin) }
#      $lockLines = @($sortedPins.Values) + @('uvloop==0.22.1; sys_platform != "win32"')
#      [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PWD 'requirements.lock'), ($lockLines -join "`n") + "`n", [Text.Encoding]::ASCII)
#      Refresh additive profile locks separately as documented; exclude base pins
#      and tzdata from their freezes, then re-add the Postgres marker to the
#      in-memory lines and write LF with WriteAllText, as in docs/DEPLOY.md.
#      Keep development/optional deps out of the base lock and review marked pins.
#   3. Run the release-lock suite and image checks, then audit every runtime profile.
#   4. Delete cleared entries. For any remaining entry, review owner=<name>,
#      expires=YYYY-MM-DD and reason=<short>; retain per-advisory reachability.
#      Do not extend an expiry without a fresh owner review.
# The next audit run re-fails if the advisory is somehow still present - the point.
#
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SEEDED 2026-08-25 (Batch-10 Train 2, gap G-08): the FIRST baseline scan of
# requirements.lock, pinned unfixed while upgrades were scheduled separately.
#
# REFRESHED 2026-09-05 (dependency refresh lock regen). The lock was
# regenerated after applying the bumps that ARE drop-in - cryptography 49.0.0->50.0.1,
# jinja2 3.1.4->3.1.6, lxml 5.3.0->6.1.2, pyasn1 0.6.3->0.6.4, python-dotenv
# 1.0.1->1.2.3, python-multipart 0.0.20->0.0.32 - so every advisory those fixed is
# DELETED here (per the "HOW TO CLEAR AN ENTRY" recipe above). Cluster status after the Pillow train:
#   * pillow - closed by the 12.3.0 bump on 2026-09-08. All 18 recorded
#     entries have fixed versions <=12.3.0. Reachable JPEG2000 advisory
#     PYSEC-2026-3496 requires 12.3.0, so 12.2.0 is insufficient.
#     A fresh network audit of all profiles remains a CI check.
#   * starlette - all seven recorded exceptions are closed by the 1.6.0 bump.
#     PYSEC-2026-1941/-1942 were already fixed by 0.52.1; the five 1.x-only
#     exceptions are closed by fixes in 1.0.1 through 1.3.1.
